preamble: Backing of the labiodental fricative [f] to the velar fricative [x] occurs in two settings. In Old Dutch, [f] before [t] became [x] (craft > kracht, after > achter), a dissimilation shared with neighbouring Low German but not with German or English. In Andalusia and parts of Spanish America, /f/ before the labial glide /w/ is articulated as an aspirate or a velar fricative (fuerte, fuego, fuente).

examples.note: Regular change ft > xt; compare German Kraft, English craft.
The obsolete variant graft preserves the older form.
Before /w/, /f/ is articulated as an aspirate or a velar fricative in Andalusia and parts of Spanish America.

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Evolution of Latin /f/ in Spanish. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_Latin_/f/_in_Spanish
